title: Sante Barley Trilogy Run Asia 2026 Davao Leg 3 Review: What the 2025 Leg 3 Was Like
seo_title: Sante Barley Trilogy Run Davao Leg 3 Review | Azuela Cove
meta_description: Sante Barley Trilogy Run Asia Davao Leg 3 review: the 2025 32K on an out-and-back course from Azuela Cove, the results, and how the 2026 series opened.
dek: The closing leg of RunRio's Davao trilogy is a 32 km out-and-back from Azuela Cove in Lanang. Here is what the 2025 edition was like, and what the 2026 series showed before Leg 3 on 27 September.
verdict: Davao Leg 3 is the long one: a 32 km centrepiece, with 21 km, 10 km and 5 km races alongside, on an out-and-back course from Azuela Cove in Lanang [1]. The 2025 edition, on 31 August, was won by Rino Satinitigan in 2:03:07 and Leedy Erika Villamonte in 2:39:49 [1]. In 2026 the series opened in March with about 2,700 runners [2], and the leg winners talked about a strong field and hard heat [2]. It is an established local series with real competition at the front, and the 32 km makes a useful supported long run before a marathon.

sections.heading: What the 2025 Leg 3 Was Like
paragraphs: The 2025 Davao Leg 3 was run on Sunday 31 August 2025 on an out-and-back course from Azuela Cove in Lanang [1]. It was the third stop of the trilogy series organised by RunRio, with KinetixSports as the local partner [1].

The 32 km was the centrepiece. Rino Satinitigan of Kidapawan City won the men's race in 2:03:07, ahead of Noel Cabrera (2:07:42) and Paul James Zafico (2:09:23), and Leedy Erika Villamonte of General Santos City won the women's in 2:39:49 [1]. Mark Luigi Joyce won the men's 21 km in 1:15:21 and Aslia Hadjiu Nassef the women's in 1:44:19 [1]. Age-group podiums were awarded down the field [1].

sections.heading: How the 2026 Series Opened
paragraphs: The 2026 Davao series began with Leg 1 at the same venue on Sunday 29 March, which about 2,700 runners joined, according to KinetixSports [2]. Elmer Bartolo won the men's 10 km in 34:38, his third straight 10 km title in the series from 2024 to 2026 [2].

The runners' own comments are the most useful guide to conditions. Bartolo said he was still worn out from the heat of the Ironman 70.3 Davao, and that there were many strong young competitors [2]. The women's 16 km winner said she had not expected to win because there were many elite runners [2]. Expect a competitive front of the race and a hot morning, even with an early start.

sections.heading: Should You Enter?
paragraphs: If you are in Mindanao and want structure in your running year, the trilogy format builds from shorter distances in Leg 1 to the 32 km in Leg 3. The same out-and-back course at Azuela Cove means you can compare your times from leg to leg.
The 32 km is the reason to pick Leg 3 in particular. Pace it for heat.
This review is compiled from published race reports on the 2025 Leg 3 and the 2026 Leg 1. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: What distances does Davao Leg 3 offer?
faqs.answer: A 32 km centrepiece race, plus a 21 km half marathon, a 10 km and a 5 km. All of them use an out-and-back course from Azuela Cove in Lanang, Davao City, the same venue as the earlier legs of the trilogy, so times are comparable from leg to leg.

faqs.question: Who won Davao Leg 3 in 2025?
faqs.answer: Rino Satinitigan won the men's 32 km in 2:03:07 and Leedy Erika Villamonte the women's in 2:39:49 on 31 August 2025. Mark Luigi Joyce and Aslia Hadjiu Nassef won the 21 km.

faqs.question: How big is the Sante Barley Trilogy Run in Davao?
faqs.answer: About 2,700 runners joined the 2026 opening leg on 29 March, according to local partner KinetixSports. The series is organised by RunRio, and the front of the race is competitive: the 2026 leg winners spoke of many strong young runners and elite athletes in the field.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-28 about the previous Leg 3 (31 August 2025), with context from the 2026 Leg 1. Replaces a pre-race preview. No report on the 27 September 2026 Leg 3 had been published when this was written. No rating: the winners' comments describe conditions, not a verdict on the event.
